title: Notion AI Autofill Database Properties: Summarize & Auto-Tag
meta_description: Set up Notion AI autofill database properties to summarize and tag requests, leads and feedback: exact steps, 3 copy-ready prompts, honest pitfalls.
quick_answer: To use Notion AI autofill on database properties, open the database, click + to add a property, and choose AI summary, AI key info or AI custom autofill. Make sure each page body contains the full text to analyze. For consistent tags, give the prompt a closed tag list and exact output format. Test on 10–20 pages, then choose auto-update or manual refresh. AI access varies by plan.
key_takeaways: Autofill reads the page, so paste the full email, form answers or review into each page body. Pages with no body text get vague results.
Use AI summary for an overview, AI key info for one named type of fact, and AI custom autofill for consistent tags.
Write tag prompts with a closed tag list, an exact output format, a fallback tag and one example. Avoid tag names that appear inside other tag names.
Refresh manually while you test. Turn on auto-update on page edits only for entries that keep changing.
Spot-check 10–20 entries before you trust the output. For decisions that matter, keep a separate final tag that only a person sets.
Check Notion's pricing page to confirm your plan includes Notion AI and whether usage is limited.
who_this_is_for: This guide is for small-business owners and operators who already keep client requests, sales leads or customer feedback in a Notion database and want AI to summarize and tag each entry so nobody has to sort them by hand.
intro: A Notion database of client requests, sales leads or customer feedback only helps if you can see what each entry says without opening it. Notion AI autofill properties can add a summary, pull out key facts and tag every row. That turns a long list of pages into something you can filter and act on. This guide walks through a real small-business setup step by step and gives you three prompts to copy. It also points out where the AI still needs a person to check its work.

steps.name: Confirm Notion AI access on your plan
steps.text: Check Notion's pricing page and your workspace settings to confirm that your plan includes Notion AI and whether AI usage is limited. Do this before you build anything your team will rely on.

steps.name: Create a page template that holds the raw text
steps.text: Click the arrow next to the database's New button, add a new template with an 'Original message' heading, and set it as the default. For every entry, paste the full email, form answers or review under that heading.

steps.name: Add an AI summary property
steps.text: Click the + at the right end of the property header row, choose AI summary from the AI options in the property type list, and name it 'AI Summary'. Generate it on a few pages to check that the summaries are the right length and focus.

steps.name: Add an AI key info property
steps.text: Add an AI key info property and say exactly what to extract, for example 'Deadline, budget and requested deliverable'. Vague instructions such as 'important details' produce vague output.

steps.name: Add an AI custom autofill property for tags
steps.text: Add an AI custom autofill property, name it 'AI Tags', and paste a prompt that includes a closed list of allowed tags, an exact output format, a fallback tag and one example of correct output.

steps.name: Test on 10–20 existing pages
steps.text: Generate results one cell at a time on a small sample and compare each tag with the one you would have chosen. Wherever the AI gets it wrong, tighten that tag's definition in the prompt and test again.

steps.name: Choose auto-update or manual refresh
steps.text: Turn on auto-update on page edits for entries that change over time, such as leads that get new call notes. Leave it off for entries that rarely change and while you're still testing. You can refresh by hand from the property's menu.

steps.name: Build filtered views and a human-owned final tag
steps.text: Create views such as 'Urgent requests' or 'Negative feedback' with a Contains or Starts with filter on the AI property. Add a 'Final Type' Select property that only your team sets, and use it for reporting and anything that matters.

sections.heading: What Notion AI autofill does (and doesn't do)
paragraphs: Notion AI autofill is a set of database property options that read each page and write an AI-generated result into a column. Summaries, extracted facts and tags appear without anyone typing them.

Three autofill types cover most small-business needs. AI summary writes a short overview of the page. AI key info pulls out one kind of information you name, such as deadlines or budgets. AI custom autofill runs an instruction you write yourself, which makes it the right choice for consistent tags. Notion also offers AI translation, which this guide doesn't cover.

Autofill works from the page content. It does best when each entry holds the raw material you want analyzed, such as a pasted client email, a lead's form answers or a customer review. If a page has only a title and a few short properties, expect thin, generic output.

Autofill writes results but doesn't take any action. It won't email a client, assign an owner or move a card by itself. If you want something to happen when a tag appears, look at Notion's own database automations or an external automation tool, and check what your plan supports.

Notion updates its interface often, so the menu labels in this guide may not exactly match yours. Newer versions may also let you switch on AI autofill for existing properties instead of only the dedicated AI types. Check Notion's help center for the current options.
bullets: AI summary: a short overview of the whole page, useful for scanning a table view.
AI key info: one named type of fact, for example 'deadline and budget'.
AI custom autofill: your own prompt, best for tags, fit ratings or suggested next actions.

sections.heading: Set up your database so autofill has something to read
paragraphs: Before you add any AI property, make sure every entry is a page with the original text inside it. Autofill output can only be as good as what the page contains.

This guide uses a Client Requests database for a small agency or service business as its running example. The same structure works for a Sales Leads or Customer Feedback database. Only the property names and prompts change.

Create a database template so every new page has the same layout. Click the arrow next to the database's New button and add a new template. Give it an 'Original message' heading with space for the pasted email or form text, plus an optional 'Team notes' heading below that. Then set it as the default template. When every page has the same structure, the AI gets the same kind of input each time, which tends to make its output more consistent.
Clean up the text before autofill runs. Put the newest message at the top and delete signatures, legal disclaimers and quoted replies. This takes seconds and reduces noise in both summaries and tags.
bullets: Request (Title): a short name, such as 'Homepage banner update – Acme'.
Client (Text, or a Relation to a Clients database).
Received (Date).
Status (Status): New, In progress, Done.
Owner (Person): who is handling the request.
Final Type (Select): the tag a person sets after reviewing the AI's suggestion. Use this one for anything you report on.

sections.heading: How to add Notion AI autofill database properties: summary, key info and custom tags
paragraphs: You add an autofill property like any other property. Open the database, click the + at the right end of the property header row, and pick the AI option you need from the property type list.

For summaries, choose AI summary and name it 'AI Summary'. Starting every AI column name with 'AI' shows your team at a glance which values a machine wrote and which a person confirmed. Once the property exists, you can generate values for a single cell or for all pages from the property's menu. The exact wording depends on your Notion version.

For key info, choose AI key info and say exactly what to extract. Good instructions are 'Deadline, budget and requested deliverable' for client requests, 'Company size, budget and timeline' for sales leads, and 'Product or order number mentioned' for feedback. 'Important details' is too vague to be useful.

For tags, choose AI custom autofill and paste in a prompt from the next section. This property delivers the most value, and it's also where most inconsistency comes from. If you already have a text column such as 'Tags', open its settings first. Recent Notion versions may let you turn on AI autofill there instead of creating a new property.
Each autofill property also has a setting that updates it automatically when a page is edited. Leave it off until you've tested your prompt. The auto-update section below explains when to turn it on.
bullets: Name AI columns clearly: 'AI Summary', 'AI Key Info', 'AI Tags'.
Give each property one job. Don't ask a single prompt to summarize, tag and score.
Hide AI columns a view doesn't need so tables stay readable.
Test on 10–20 existing pages before running it on the whole database.

sections.heading: Three ready-to-copy prompts for consistent AI tags
paragraphs: Consistent tags come from prompts with four parts: a closed list of allowed values, an exact output format, a fallback for unclear cases, and one example of correct output.

Without those four parts, the same kind of request might be tagged 'Bug', 'Bug fix' and 'Technical issue' on different pages, and your filters stop working. With them, the text property is predictable enough to filter. For example, a Contains filter can show every row where AI Tags contains 'Urgent'.

Choose tag names that never appear inside one another. A Contains filter matches partial text, so a filter for 'Bug' would also match 'Bug Fix'. 'Positive' and 'Negative' are safe as a pair, but avoid pairs like 'Lead' and 'Hot Lead'. If the tag comes first in the output, a Starts with filter is even more precise.

Test a prompt on a message where you already know the right answer. For example, an email that says 'Our checkout button stopped working this morning and customers can't pay' should come back as 'Bug | Urgent'. If it doesn't, rewrite the definition of Urgent in the prompt.

Once a prompt works, don't edit it casually. Even small wording changes can shift how existing categories get applied. If you do change it, rerun your test pages and compare the results before you update the whole database.
To use a prompt, replace the bracketed parts with your own services or categories. Then paste everything after the colon into the custom autofill property.
bullets: Client requests (property: AI Tags): Classify this client request. Choose exactly one Type from: Bug, Change Request, New Project, Billing, Question, Other. Choose exactly one Urgency from: Urgent, Normal, Low. Use Urgent only if the client mentions a deadline within 7 days, something broken or down for their customers, or lost revenue. Output only: Type | Urgency. Example: Change Request | Normal. No explanations and no extra words. If the request is unclear, output: Other | Normal.

Sales leads (property: AI Lead Fit): Assess this sales lead using only information on this page. Choose one Fit from: Hot, Warm, Cold, Not a fit. Hot = mentions a budget AND a timeline within 90 days. Warm = clear need but no budget or no timeline. Cold = general enquiry with no specific need. Not a fit = asks for something outside our services: [list your services]. Output only: Fit — next action in 12 words or fewer. Example: Warm — Send pricing guide and ask about their timeline. Do not invent budgets, dates or company details. If key information is missing, make the next action about asking for it.

Customer feedback (property: AI Feedback Tags): Tag this customer feedback. Choose one Sentiment from: Positive, Neutral, Negative. Choose up to two Themes from: Pricing, Delivery, Product Quality, Support, Website, Feature Request. If no theme fits, use Other. Output only: Sentiment; Theme, Theme. Example: Negative; Delivery, Support. Use the words exactly as written in these lists. No explanations.
Filter tip: for the leads prompt, filter AI Lead Fit with Starts with 'Hot'. Don't use Contains, because the next-action text could include the same word.

sections.heading: Auto-update on page edits vs manual refresh: which to choose
paragraphs: Choose auto-update on page edits if entries keep changing and the AI output needs to stay current. Choose manual refresh if pages are mostly final, if you're still testing a prompt, or if you want tighter control over AI usage.

With auto-update on, Notion regenerates the value after a page is edited, though not always instantly. This suits a sales leads database where you add call notes over time and want the Lead Fit tag to reflect the latest conversation.

With auto-update off, values change only when someone triggers an update, for a single cell or for all pages from the property's menu. This suits customer feedback, which rarely changes once it's logged. It's also the safer setting while you refine a prompt, because you decide when results get overwritten.

Watch for one common trap. If a teammate corrects an AI tag by hand while auto-update is on, a later edit to the page may regenerate the value and erase the correction. Keep AI suggestions and human decisions in separate columns. 'AI Tags' makes the suggestion, and a 'Final Type' Select property that only the owner sets holds the decision.

If your plan limits AI usage, auto-update on a large, busy database will use more of it than occasional manual refreshes. Check Notion's pricing and help pages to see how autofill counts toward any limits.
bullets: Auto-update on: sales leads with ongoing notes, active projects, requests that change over time.
Manual refresh: feedback logs, archived records, prompt testing, large batches of older entries.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting and honest trade-offs before you rely on AI tags
paragraphs: Notion AI autofill saves sorting time, but you can't set it and forget it. Tags need spot-checks, long pages can be summarized poorly, and access depends on your Notion plan.

AI tags need spot-checks. Even with a tight prompt, the AI will sometimes pick a category that sounds right but isn't, especially when a message mixes two issues. Review every result in your test batch, then check a handful of entries each week. If the same tag keeps going wrong, tighten its definition in the prompt instead of fixing rows one by one.

Long pages may be summarized poorly. With long email threads, meeting transcripts or pages full of embedded blocks, summaries can skip details or give too much weight to whatever comes first. Trim the page, put the key message at the top, and split very long threads into separate entries. Use AI key info for facts you can't afford to miss.

Extra words in a tag column usually mean the prompt is too loose. If you see explanations, inconsistent spellings or tags outside your list, add 'Output only' and 'Use the words exactly as written in these lists' to the prompt, and make sure the example matches the format exactly.

Notion AI access depends on your plan. Notion has changed how it packages AI more than once, with plan-based inclusion, trials and add-ons at different times. Confirm the current details on Notion's pricing page before you build workflows your team depends on.

Consider how sensitive your data is. Autofill sends page content to Notion's AI features for processing. Before you run it on confidential client information, read Notion's published AI and security documentation and check your workspace admin settings.

This setup isn't a good fit if your data lives mainly outside Notion. If your leads are in a CRM or your tickets are in a helpdesk, copying them into Notion just to tag them leaves you with duplicate records to keep in sync. Check whether those tools have their own AI tagging first.
bullets: First week: review every AI tag in your test batch.
Ongoing: check a sample each week, and fix the prompt rather than individual rows.
Before rollout: confirm your plan, any AI usage limits and Notion's data policies on its site.

sections.heading: Getting requests, leads and feedback into Notion automatically
paragraphs: Autofill only helps if new entries arrive with their full text, so the last piece is a reliable way to get them into the database.

The simplest built-in option is a Notion form connected to your database, if your plan and workspace support it. Each submission becomes a page, and the answers are saved as properties. Answers may end up in properties rather than the page body, so send a few test submissions and confirm that autofill picks up the details you care about.

If requests arrive by email, website chat or another tool's form, an automation tool such as Zapier or Make can create a Notion page for each one and put the message text in the page body. Zapier is usually quicker to set up for simple flows. Make's visual builder suits multi-step or higher-volume flows and is often cheaper at scale. Compare current pricing on both sites against your expected volume.

After you connect any automation, check whether autofill runs on the pages it creates. If it doesn't, either run a manual update on all pages at a set time each day, or turn on auto-update and confirm the behavior with a few test entries.
bullets: Map the message text to the page body, not just to a short property.
Map sender, date and source to regular properties so you can filter on them.
Add a 'Source' Select property (Form, Email, Chat) so you can compare channels later.

recommendations.best_for: Small teams that already keep client requests, sales leads or customer feedback in Notion databases and want AI summaries and tags in the same workspace. Confirm on Notion's pricing page that your plan includes Notion AI and check any usage limits.
recommendations.not_for: Teams whose customer data lives mainly in a dedicated CRM or helpdesk. Copying it into Notion just to tag it creates duplicate records, and those tools often have their own AI features.

recommendations.best_for: Sending form submissions, emails or chat messages into a Notion database automatically, with the full text in the page body so autofill has something to read. It needs very little setup for simple one-step flows.
recommendations.not_for: Teams that already capture everything inside Notion, for example with Notion forms. It's also not ideal for very high-volume flows, where usage-based pricing can add up. Check current pricing first.

recommendations.best_for: Multi-step or higher-volume intake workflows into Notion, where a visual builder and potentially lower cost at scale matter. Confirm current pricing for your volume.
recommendations.not_for: Beginners who want the simplest possible setup, or anyone moving only a handful of entries a week.

faq.question: Is Notion AI autofill included in every Notion plan?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Access to Notion AI depends on your plan, and Notion has changed how it packages AI over time, with trials, plan-based inclusion and add-ons at different times. Check Notion's pricing page for current details and usage limits before you build workflows around autofill.

faq.question: Does Notion AI autofill update automatically when I edit a page?
faq.answer: Only if you turn on auto-update on page edits for that property. With it on, Notion regenerates the value after the page is edited, though not always instantly. With it off, you update a single cell or all pages by hand from the property's menu.

faq.question: How do I get consistent tags from Notion AI autofill?
faq.answer: Use a custom autofill prompt with a closed list of allowed tags, an exact output format, a fallback tag such as 'Other', and one example of correct output. Choose tag names that don't appear inside one another so Contains filters work reliably. Test on 10–20 pages, tighten definitions wherever tags drift, and keep a separate Select property that a person sets for final decisions.

faq.question: Can Notion AI autofill fill a Select or Multi-select property?
faq.answer: AI autofill started out producing text, and newer versions of Notion have expanded where you can use it. Open the settings of a Select or Multi-select property in your workspace and see whether an AI autofill option appears. If it doesn't, write the tags to a text property and filter with Contains or Starts with.

faq.question: Does Notion AI autofill work on database entries I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. After you add an autofill property, you can generate values for existing pages one cell at a time or for all pages from the property's menu. On a large database, test on 10–20 pages before updating everything, especially if your plan limits AI usage.

faq.question: Why is my Notion AI summary vague or missing details?
faq.answer: Usually the page either has very little content or is very long. Autofill reads the page, so an empty page body gives generic output, and long threads can be summarized poorly. Trim signatures and quoted replies, put the key message first, and use AI key info for facts you have to capture.

conclusion: Notion AI autofill works best on a simple setup: each page holds the original text, each AI property has one job, and tag prompts use a closed list with an exact output format. Start with AI summary and AI key info for quick scanning. Then add one custom autofill property using the prompt that matches your database. Test it on a small batch and refresh manually until the tags stay consistent. Turn on auto-update only where entries keep changing, and keep a person in charge of the final tag on anything that affects money or clients. Before you rely on any of this, confirm your plan's current Notion AI access and usage limits on Notion's site.
